title: arXiv Biology & Biomedicine — Daily Brief (27 October 2026)
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart or readership statistics. This is a relevance-ranked selection from an incomplete biomedical preprint corpus; bioRxiv, medRxiv, and the wider medical literature are not covered. Attention and verified citation signals are sparse, so no popularity ranking is implied.

sections.title: Headline
sections.abstract: The latest 27 October announcement batch contains six verifiable biology and biomedical papers in the configured arXiv categories. The strongest pattern is computational methods tied to experimental or measurement work—DNA read reconstruction, label-free live-cell imaging, and radionuclide production—alongside cardiovascular and cell-growth models. The list is relevance-ranked, not a popularity chart.

sections.title: ACOR: incremental evidence accumulation towards real-time DNA storage reconstruction
sections.abstract: ACOR incrementally accumulates evidence from sequencing reads and reconstructs DNA-storage sequences at cluster closure, with tests on simulated and real datasets including the authors’ own short-read NGS library.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 99.9844% exact reconstruction at k=15 on their full NGS library of 96,055 designed sequences, using assigned read observations. ACOR records k-mer transition and boundary evidence incrementally before a single consensus decoding step.
sections.unique_caveat: Current evaluations receive already-assigned clusters, known design lengths, and externally determined cluster closure; therefore they do not yet test an end-to-end live pipeline. Difficult long-sequence errors and reference-free parameter selection remain open issues.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in genomics; reports real and simulated DNA-storage evaluations, including a wet-lab NGS library with 96,055 designed sequences and 17.7 million assigned read observations.

sections.title: Video-rate quantitative phase and polarimetric imaging (QP2I) for label-free imaging of contracting muscle cells
sections.abstract: QP2I combines quantitative phase and polarimetric imaging in a single-shot, video-rate setup based on a differential-interference-contrast microscope and polarization camera, demonstrated on reference targets, fixed tissue, and live cardiomyocytes.
sections.claimed_contribution: The preprint combines a regularized phase-reconstruction method with Stokes-based retardance reconstruction to provide structural and functional optical readouts, including sarcomere length and retardance changes during contraction.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is optical-method validation and cell-level demonstration, not clinical testing. The authors note phase-gradient wrapping, ambiguities in strongly birefringent samples, and reduced effective resolution from the polarization-camera pixel arrangement.
sections.announcement_type: revision (v3; first submitted 23 October 2026), 27 October 2026 batch
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Substantive v3 revision in the batch; authors report validation on simulations, reference targets, fixed muscle tissue, and living cells, with video-rate acquisition reported up to 70 fps.

sections.title: Optimization of 99mTc proton-induced production by means of cross-section measurements of technetium radioisotopes from molybdenum targets
sections.abstract: The authors measure proton-induced reaction cross-sections on solid molybdenum targets and use them to assess technetium radionuclide production and optimize a cyclotron-based route to 99mTc.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors identify approximately 16 MeV protons and a roughly 0.5 mm highly enriched 100Mo target as suitable conditions. They calculate about 1.7 GBq/μA after a 10-hour irradiation while estimating radionuclidic purity within European Pharmacopoeia limits.
sections.unique_caveat: The yield is calculated from the study’s measurements and production tests are feasibility evidence; this does not establish routine-scale supply, clinical deployment, or patient outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in medical physics; the paper reports measured reaction cross-sections and production tests, rather than only a computational proposal.

sections.title: Bodyseismography (BSG): Theoretical Foundation and Numerical Modeling
sections.abstract: BSG models how cardiac excitation and body/bed transmission jointly shape contactless cardiovascular vibration measurements, with participant-specific numerical modeling and controlled stroke-volume perturbations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report median Pearson correlations of 0.865 (vertical) and 0.682 (planar-sum) for matched-window waveform reconstruction; modeled transmission reversed a vertical feature association in 8 of 27 participant-specific transfer models.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a theoretical and numerical modeling study, not prospective clinical validation of stroke volume, cardiac output, or blood-pressure measurement. The reported correlations concern waveform reconstruction in the modeled setting.
sections.announcement_type: revision (v2; first submitted 26 October 2026), 27 October 2026 batch
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Substantive v2 revision; the numerical analysis covers 27 participants and reports matched-window waveform correlations for vertical and planar-sum channels.

sections.title: Multiscale MIGHT: Modeling Local and Systemic Particle Transport in the Cardiovascular System
sections.abstract: Multiscale MIGHT models signaling-molecule transport through branched local vessels and closed-loop systemic circulation, incorporating organ clearance and chemical degradation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The model joins vessel-level topology with a whole-body circulation representation. Simulations predict that later recirculation passes become dispersed and are governed mainly by systemic organ clearance and degradation rather than local vessel geometry.
sections.unique_caveat: Validation is against numerical simulation, while whole-body examples are model-based; the paper does not report biological tracer experiments. The systemic circulation is represented with lumped organ blocks outside the detailed local network.
sections.announcement_type: revision (v2; first submitted 26 October 2026), 27 October 2026 batch
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Substantive v2 revision; the authors compare the closed-loop approximation against COMSOL finite-element simulations and report whole-body simulations across transmitter locations and signaling-molecule species. The arXiv comment says the work was submitted to IEEE ICC 2027.

sections.title: Stationary Action Principles for Neuronal Growth
sections.abstract: The paper develops stochastic and mechanics-based variational models for axonal growth on patterned or stiffness-varying substrates, predicting most-probable paths and turning behavior at stiffness boundaries.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors derive a stochastic path action for growth on periodic micropatterns and a Fermat-like action for stiffness-dependent traction, including an approximate Snell-like relation and critical-angle condition.
sections.unique_caveat: These are theoretical/model-derived predictions, not new neuronal-growth experiments. The stochastic and quasi-static descriptions have distinct assumptions and validity regimes, so experimental agreement remains to be established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across cell behavior, quantitative biology, and neuronal research; the contribution offers explicit, testable trajectory predictions linking drift, diffusion, substrate stiffness, traction, and growth direction.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.abstract: Recurring motifs in this small selection are computation paired with biological measurement; models connecting local measurements to system-level cardiovascular biology; and mechanics shaping biological trajectories or signals. These are corpus-level similarities, not evidence of a field-wide shift.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.abstract: Follow-up work includes testing ACOR with online read assignment and reference-free settings; evaluating QP2I ambiguities across more cell types and against orthogonal assays; replicating 99mTc production measurements across cyclotrons; testing BSG on held-out cohorts with reference hemodynamic measurements; comparing MIGHT predictions with controlled tracer experiments; and testing neuronal-growth path predictions on stiffness-gradient substrates.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.abstract: The batch connects computation with biological or physical measurements, but evidence ranges from wet-lab sequencing and cell demonstrations to production tests, numerical modeling, and theory. Independent validation under more complete biological conditions remains a shared need; no popularity ranking is supported.
